repetitions: 5 independent full runs, 30 reps/query round-robin-interleaved within each, 200x-batched for A/B/B2

headline_result.B_vs_A_p50_overhead: +63.03% to +64.50% across 5 runs -- DOES NOT PASS <=5% target
headline_result.B_per_query_allocs: 4 (vs A's 2) -- localizes B's overhead to a 2-String tuple-key clone per lookup
headline_result.B2_per_query_allocs: 2 (identical to A) -- confirms the redesign eliminates the allocation, not just hides it
headline_result.methodology_corrections: two, disclosed in full in ISSUE38_LOG.md: (1) unbatched sub-microsecond timing produced a sign flip on B's overhead between two runs (+19% vs -15%), fixed via 200x call-batching for A/B/B2 and raising reps to 30; (2) an adversarial check found the batch loops lacked std::hint::black_box, letting the lto=true/codegen-units=1 release profile potentially treat repeated identical calls as partly redundant -- adding black_box corrected the magnitudes (B: ~75%->~63-65%; B2: ~-10-13%->~-5-6%) without changing either verdict
headline_result.gate_verdict: E1 PASSES via the redesigned B2 compiled-schema representation; the naive B design's failure was implementation-specific (an avoidable per-query allocation), not fundamental, exactly the redesign-and-retest Issue #38 asks for
